payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to suppress negative-electrolyte crossover, a key aging pathway in sodium-flow systems. Independent auditing corrected the cell’s cycle life to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold; the earlier 12,000 claim was retracted because it used un-normalized depth-of-discharge data. The chemistry delivers 148 Wh/kg gravimetric energy density. At projected 500 MWh manufacturing scale, its stack-level cost is $61/kWh. Its principal operational limitation is a 4 °C temperature floor, below which the dopant precipitates and cycling must stop.
